input: Negotiate the freelance contract rate before signing

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is about rate alone or other contract terms (payment schedule, revision limits, kill fees) changes what needs to be negotiated and prepared.
The counterpart — a direct client, a recruiter, or an agency — determines tone, leverage dynamics, and who has authority to approve a rate change.
Whether the user has already received an offer, is pre-offer, or is mid-negotiation sets which stage the plan should start from.
The user's minimum acceptable rate and any hard deadline to respond create the boundaries within which a strategy must operate.
Whether the user prefers to negotiate via email, phone, or in person — and how assertive they want to be — shapes the communication approach and scripts needed.
Knowing the target rate (or % increase) the user is aiming for defines what a win looks like and when to stop pushing.
Understanding the user's current rate relative to market, their experience level, and the project type informs the specific arguments and data points to use.

gold.taskTitle: Negotiate freelance contract rate before signing
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to successfully negotiate their freelance contract rate with a client before committing to and signing the agreement.

questions.title: Is this about rate only, or other contract terms too?
questions.description: Clarify whether the negotiation scope is limited to the hourly or project rate, or whether it also includes payment terms, revision clauses, kill fees, or IP ownership.

questions.title: Who exactly are you negotiating with — client, recruiter, or agency?
questions.description: Identify the counterpart to tailor leverage, tone, and escalation strategy appropriately.

questions.title: Where in the process are you — offer received, or still pre-offer?
questions.description: Determine the current negotiation stage to know whether to initiate, counter, or hold firm.

questions.title: What is the deadline to respond or sign the contract?
questions.description: Establish any hard time constraints that limit how long the negotiation can run and when the user must commit.

questions.title: Do you prefer to negotiate over email, phone, or in person?
questions.description: Determine the preferred communication channel to prepare the right scripts, talking points, or written templates.

questions.title: What specific rate are you aiming to land at?
questions.description: Pin down the target number or percentage increase so the plan has a clear definition of a successful outcome.

questions.title: What rate were you offered, and what is your field or specialty?
questions.description: Capture the current offer and the user's domain to benchmark against market rates and build concrete justification arguments.
